objective: M1 tier A (docs/m1-criteria.md section 8): can the player character's world position be observed reproducibly from what the pinned GOG build exposes by itself (its own text files, read read-only), without changing anything in the game, its files, its saves or its process, while network monitoring covers the whole run?
hypothesis: Tier A INCONCLUSIVE / NO DATA: no permitted file contains the player position, because the game writes no log file (F-ENV-014) and its config files hold settings. This is an expectation fixed before the run, not a result. The session gates are expected to hold: build check 0 at start and end, nothing removed, nothing written outside GAME_WRITTEN, a clean exit through the menu. No expectation is predeclared for the network verdict: any contact by the game is recorded and is a FAIL (stop condition 4).
environment: Windows 11 Pro x64, Python 3.15, logman and tracerpt from Windows; the owner's pinned GOG set (D-008 amended), launched directly with GOG Galaxy and Steam closed
procedure: Only after the owner's explicit approval of docs/m1-criteria.md section 8. Per session N: the owner copies the saves aside offline, closes GOG Galaxy and Steam, opens an elevated PowerShell in the repository and runs python -I tools/m1/tier_a.py --session N. The tool refuses without elevation, with Galaxy, Steam or the game running, or without the backup confirmation. It runs check_gog_build (exit 0 needed, else NOT RUN), snapshots user = %LOCALAPPDATA%/WB Games/Shadow of War (SHA-256; saves hashed, never read) and install = the GOG folder (size and modification time), and starts the network trace. The owner launches the game, loads a save, stands in an open place and presses Enter in the console; t=0 is 10 s later. One beep: stand still 0-30 s. Two beeps: walk forward without stopping 30-60 s. Three beeps: done; the owner quits through the game's menu. The tool waits for the exit, asks whether the game was closed through its menu, showed any integrity, tamper or debugger warning, or crashed; stops and analyzes the trace for ShadowOfWar.exe and its children (raw trace deleted); re-runs the build check and the snapshots; reads the permitted text files (.cfg .ini .log .txt .json .xml .nfo up to 4 MB in both roots, never .sav, never x64) read-only for a labelled position triple (pos/position/loc/location then three numbers) with a clock time on the same line; and classifies with session.classify. GAME_WRITTEN = user/*_ShadowOfWar.sav, user/render.cfg, user/gpu.nfo; anything else added or changed (CloudStorage, the install) is an unexpected write. Tolerances: still_max 0.5, move_min 5.0 (game units), min_obs 3. Evidence: evidence/logs/m1-tier-a-<time>-s<N>/session.json, with no local paths, machine or user names, or save ids. Order: session 1 first. If it ends Tier A INCONCLUSIVE / NO DATA with every other gate sound, tier A ends there (section 3) and no further session is run. M1 go needs 3 PASS sessions. Any FAIL or other INCONCLUSIVE stops the series and goes back to the owner. Review #36 changes (FB-36-01/03/05/06): the install's permitted text files are hashed at both ends, its other files by size and modification time only (a low-assurance change signal, not proof of unchanged content); a save under an id that had no save before the session is an unexpected write (FAIL); a failed trace analysis is recorded as monitoring that did not cover the session; session.json records no_data_established, true only when the session is INCONCLUSIVE and no position is its only reason, so a session with failed monitoring or evidence cannot close tier A. Codex pass 7 changes: permitted files are read as UTF-8 (BOM or not) or UTF-16 with a BOM, any other encoding is unreadable evidence; only whole save names establish an existing id (a .sav.bak does not); save ids are redacted inside longer names too; before each session the tool stops the trace and deletes any earlier session's temporary folder, and refuses to start if a raw file there cannot be deleted.
expected_result: Session 1 ends INCONCLUSIVE with the reason 'no data: no position observed (Tier A INCONCLUSIVE / NO DATA)' and no FAIL reason. no_data_established is true.
observed_result: Session 1 ran on 2026-10-28, the owner's elevated run of the tool at 757ac6a (clean): evidence/logs/m1-tier-a-2026-10-28-113203-s1/session.json. Outcome INCONCLUSIVE; no_data_established is false. The session gates held: build check exit 0 at start and at end; nothing removed; every added or changed file is in GAME_WRITTEN (three existing saves changed, one new slot added under an id that already had saves, so not a new id); the game's start and exit were inside the trace, exit code 0, closed through its menu; the owner reported no integrity, tamper or debugger warning and no crash; both canaries were seen; no contact and no DNS lookup was attributed to the game; the raw trace was deleted. No position was observed: 0 observations in each action, from the 6 permitted files that were read. Two further reasons kept the session from establishing NO DATA: (1) ETW reported 1203 lost events, so network monitoring did not cover the session (condition 9) and the absence of contacts is not established; (2) two permitted files were unreadable under the predeclared encoding rule: install/EULA.txt and user/gpu.nfo. Diagnosis after the run, from byte statistics only (no content recorded): EULA.txt has no BOM and no NUL byte, 100 bytes at or above 0x80, is not valid UTF-8 and decodes as Windows-1252 (a legacy-encoded text file); gpu.nfo is 208 bytes of which 134 are NUL (a binary file with a .nfo extension). As predeclared, this other INCONCLUSIVE stops the series and goes back to the owner.
errors: The expected result was not met: no_data_established is false because of 1203 lost ETW events and two unreadable permitted files. The trace runs with logman's default buffers; EXP-046 provoked lost events only with tiny buffers on a stand-in process, so buffer sizing for a real session was never measured. The encoding rule (Codex pass 7) did not anticipate a Windows-1252 text file or a binary file with a .nfo extension.
follow_up: Back to the owner (predeclared). Proposed, not done: (a) larger ETW buffers in netwatch.start, measured elevated with coverage.py on a stand-in before any further session; (b) a decision on the two files, for example: read a permitted file with no BOM and no NUL byte that is not UTF-8 as Windows-1252, and treat user/gpu.nfo as a game-written binary file that is hashed but not scanned. Both change section 8 and the session tools, so they need review and a new approval by the owner before session 2. Tier B is never started by this experiment.
